title: gateway oscore stores: corrupt (not missing) record permanently bricks the context - heal covers only missing records
description: Found by 3x codereview of the recipient-store heal (9liz), robustness pass. FileStorage::write is atomic (0600 exclusive temp, fsync, verify, rename, dir fsync - lichen-hal/src/storage.rs:536-558), so torn records are only reachable via external causes (bitrot, tampering, hand-planted files). A corrupt state or floor record makes read() return Err(Corrupt) (gateway.rs:361-362) which propagates out of load() before the match arms: the heal handles MISSING records (state without floor / floor lag), never corrupt ones. A context with a bitrotted floor is Err(Corrupt) on every call forever (fail-closed, no security issue; availability trade-off only). Decide the intended policy: keep fail-closed-by-design (document it) vs add a bounded recovery path (e.g. corrupt floor + valid state heals like the missing-floor arm, since the seal is unforgeable; corrupt state + valid floor stays fatal). If healing corrupt floors, the same-highest window-bit argument still requires copying the exact sealed state.
